sanskrit: amedhyamadhye vasati māṃsaśoṇitalepane tatas tu vāyuvegena ūrdhvapādo hy adhaḥśirāḥ
english: It dwells amid filth, smeared with flesh and blood; and then, driven by the force of the wind, it turns feet upward and head downward.

sanskrit: yonidvāram upāgamya bahūn kleśān samṛcchati yonisaṃpīḍanāc caiva pūrvakarmabhir anvitaḥ
english: Reaching the door of the womb, it meets with many torments, crushed in the passage of birth and bound to the deeds of its former lives.

sanskrit: tasmān muktaḥ sa saṃsārād anyān paśyaty upadravān grahās tam upasarpanti sārameyā ivāmiṣam
english: Freed from that round of the womb, he beholds yet other afflictions; the seizing planets steal upon him as hounds upon a piece of meat.

sanskrit: tataḥ prāptottare kāle vyādhayaś cāpi taṃ tathā upasarpanti jīvantaṃ badhyamānaṃ svakarmabhiḥ
english: Then, when the later season of his life has come, diseases too steal upon him as he lives, bound fast by his own deeds.

sanskrit: baddham indriyapāśais taṃ saṅgasvādubhir āturam vyasanāny upavartante vividhāni narādhipa badhyamānaś ca tair bhūyo naiva tṛptim upaiti saḥ
english: Bound by the nooses of the senses, made sick by the sweetness of attachments, calamities of every kind beset him, O lord of men; and bound the tighter by them, he attains no satisfaction at all.

sanskrit: ayaṃ na budhyate tāvad yamalokam athāgatam yamadūtair vikṛṣyaṃś ca mṛtyuṃ kālena gacchati
english: He does not so much as perceive that the realm of Yama has now drawn near; and dragged off by Yama's messengers, in due time he goes to his death.

sanskrit: vāgghīnasya ca yanmātram iṣṭāniṣṭaṃ kṛtaṃ mukhe bhūya evātmanātmānaṃ badhyamānam upekṣate
english: Whatever pleasing or unpleasing words were spoken in his presence when he had lost his speech — he heeds them not, even as by his own self he binds his own self ever more.

sanskrit: aho vinikṛto loko lobhena ca vaśīkṛtaḥ lobhakrodhamadonmatto nātmānam avabudhyate
english: Ah, how the world is deceived and made the thrall of greed! Maddened by greed, by wrath, and by pride, it does not come to know its own self.

sanskrit: kulīnatvena ramate duṣkulīnān vikutsayan dhanadarpeṇa dṛptaś ca daridrān parikutsayan
english: He delights in his high birth and reviles the low-born; puffed up with the arrogance of wealth, he heaps scorn upon the poor.

sanskrit: mūrkhān iti parān āha nātmānaṃ samavekṣate śikṣāṃ kṣipati cānyeṣāṃ nātmānaṃ śāstum icchati
english: He calls others fools, yet looks not upon himself; he flings instruction at all others, but has no wish to school his own self.

sanskrit: adhruve jīvaloke 'smin yo dharmam anupālayan janmaprabhṛti varteta prāpnuyāt paramāṃ gatim
english: Whoever, in this unstable world of the living, abides from his very birth in the keeping of dharma — he shall attain the highest goal.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvaṃ viditvā vai yas tattvam anuvartate sa pramokṣāya labhate panthānaṃ manujādhipa
english: Thus having understood all things, whoever follows after the truth gains the path that leads to liberation, O lord of men.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yad idaṃ dharmagahanaṃ buddhyā samanugamyate etad vistaraśaḥ sarvaṃ buddhimārgaṃ praśaṃsa me
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: This thicket of dharma that is pursued through the intellect — expound to me at length, in its fullness, this whole path of wisdom.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca atra te vartayiṣyāmi namaskṛtvā svayaṃbhuve yathā saṃsāragahanaṃ vadanti paramarṣayaḥ
english: Vidura said: On this I shall instruct you, having first bowed to the Self-Existent, telling how the supreme seers describe the thicket of worldly existence.

sanskrit: kaś cin mahati saṃsāre vartamāno dvijaḥ kila vanaṃ durgam anuprāpto mahat kravyādasaṃkulam
english: A certain brāhmaṇa, faring on within this vast round of existence, came, it is said, to a great and impassable forest, thronged with beasts that feed on flesh.

sanskrit: siṃhavyāghragajākārair atighorair mahāśanaiḥ samantāt saṃparikṣiptaṃ mṛtyor api bhayapradam
english: Hemmed in on every side by creatures shaped like lions, tigers, and elephants — most fearsome, great-jawed devourers — it struck terror even into Death himself.

sanskrit: tad asya dṛṣṭvā hṛdayam udvegam agamat param abhyucchrayaś ca romṇāṃ vai vikriyāś ca paraṃtapa
english: Beholding this, his heart fell into the utmost dread; his hair stood on end, and his whole frame was thrown into agitation, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: sa tad vanaṃ vyanusaran vipradhāvan itas tataḥ vīkṣamāṇo diśaḥ sarvāḥ śaraṇaṃ kva bhaved iti
english: Roaming that forest, running this way and that, he gazed about him in every direction, wondering where a refuge might be found.

sanskrit: sa teṣāṃ chidram anvicchan pradruto bhayapīḍitaḥ na ca niryāti vai dūraṃ na ca tair viprayujyate
english: Seeking some gap between those beasts, he fled on, oppressed by fear; yet he could win no distance away, nor break free of them.

sanskrit: athāpaśyad vanaṃ ghoraṃ samantād vāgurāvṛtam bāhubhyāṃ saṃpariṣvaktaṃ striyā paramaghorayā
english: Then he saw that the dreadful forest was hedged about on every side with a net, and was enfolded within the two arms of a most terrible woman.

sanskrit: pañcaśīrṣadharair nāgaiḥ śailair iva samunnataiḥ nabhaḥspṛśair mahāvṛkṣaiḥ parikṣiptaṃ mahāvanam
english: That great forest was ringed about by five-headed serpents, towering like mountains, and by mighty trees that brushed against the sky.

sanskrit: vanamadhye ca tatrābhūd udapānaḥ samāvṛtaḥ vallībhis tṛṇachannābhir gūḍhābhir abhisaṃvṛtaḥ
english: And there in the midst of the forest was a well, all overgrown, hidden and encircled by creepers covered over with grass.

sanskrit: papāta sa dvijas tatra nigūḍhe salilāśaye vilagnaś cābhavat tasmiṃl latāsaṃtānasaṃkaṭe
english: Into that concealed reservoir of water the brāhmaṇa fell, and there he hung, caught fast in the tangled mesh of creepers.

sanskrit: panasasya yathā jātaṃ vṛntabaddhaṃ mahāphalam sa tathā lambate tatra ūrdhvapādo hy adhaḥśirāḥ
english: As a great jackfruit grows bound by its stalk, so did he hang there, his feet upward and his head below.

sanskrit: atha tatrāpi cānyo 'sya bhūyo jāta upadravaḥ kūpavīnāhavelāyām apaśyata mahāgajam
english: Then there too another affliction yet arose for him: at the rim about the mouth of the well he saw a mighty elephant.

sanskrit: ṣaḍvaktraṃ kṛṣṇaśabalaṃ dviṣaṭkapadacāriṇam krameṇa parisarpantaṃ vallīvṛkṣasamāvṛtam
english: Six-faced it was, dark and dappled, moving upon twelve feet, creeping on by degrees, wrapped about with creepers and trees.

sanskrit: tasya cāpi praśākhāsu vṛkṣaśākhāvalambinaḥ nānārūpā madhukarā ghorarūpā bhayāvahāḥ āsate madhu saṃbhṛtya pūrvam eva niketajāḥ
english: And upon the boughs of that tree, clinging to its branches, were bees of many kinds, dreadful of form and fearful to behold, settled there, having gathered honey before, born of the hive.

sanskrit: bhūyo bhūyaḥ samīhante madhūni bharatarṣabha svādanīyāni bhūtānāṃ na yair bālo 'pi tṛpyate
english: Again and again they crave the honey, O bull of the Bhāratas — honey so sweet to all creatures that not even a child is sated by it.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ madhūnāṃ bahudhā dhārā prasravate sadā tāṃ lambamānaḥ sa pumān dhārāṃ pibati sarvadā na cāsya tṛṣṇā viratā pibamānasya saṃkaṭe
english: From that honey a stream flows down forever in many a trickle; and that man, hanging there, drinks of the stream without ceasing, yet his thirst is not stilled as he drinks on in his plight.

sanskrit: abhīpsati ca tāṃ nityam atṛptaḥ sa punaḥ punaḥ na cāsya jīvite rājan nirvedaḥ samajāyata
english: Unsated, he longs for it still, again and again; and yet, O king, no aversion to life was ever born in him.

sanskrit: tatraiva ca manuṣyasya jīvitāśā pratiṣṭhitā kṛṣṇāḥ śvetāś ca taṃ vṛkṣaṃ kuṭṭayanti sma mūṣakāḥ
english: There still the man's hope of life stands fixed, while black mice and white gnaw away at that very tree.

sanskrit: vyālaiś ca vanadurgānte striyā ca paramograyā kūpādhastāc ca nāgena vīnāhe kuñjareṇa ca
english: From the beasts of prey at the forest's impassable edge, from the most terrible woman, from the serpent at the bottom of the well, and from the elephant at its rim —

sanskrit: vṛkṣaprapātāc ca bhayaṃ mūṣakebhyaś ca pañcamam madhulobhān madhukaraiḥ ṣaṣṭham āhur mahad bhayam
english: there is danger; and danger too from the falling of the tree, and the fifth from the mice; and the sixth great danger, they say, comes from the bees through his greed for honey.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa vasate tatra kṣiptaḥ saṃsārasāgare na caiva jīvitāśāyāṃ nirvedam upagacchati
english: Thus does he dwell there, cast into the ocean of worldly existence, and yet he comes to no weariness of his hope for life.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca aho khalu mahad duḥkhaṃ kṛcchravāsaṃ vasaty asau kathaṃ tasya ratis tatra tuṣṭir vā vadatāṃ vara
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Ah, surely it is a great misery — in such anguish does he dwell! How can there be any delight or contentment for him there, O best of speakers?

sanskrit: sa deśaḥ kva nu yatrāsau vasate dharmasaṃkaṭe kathaṃ vā sa vimucyeta naras tasmān mahābhayāt
english: Where then is that place in which he dwells, hard pressed in the matter of dharma? And how might that man be released from that great peril?

sanskrit: etan me sarvam ācakṣva sādhu ceṣṭāmahe tathā kṛpā me mahatī jātā tasyābhyuddharaṇena hi
english: Tell me all of this, that we may rightly strive thus; for a great compassion has arisen in me to deliver him.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca upamānam idaṃ rājan mokṣavidbhir udāhṛtam sugatiṃ vindate yena paralokeṣu mānavaḥ
english: Vidura said: This is a parable, O king, set forth by those who know the way of release, whereby a man finds a happy goal in the worlds beyond.

sanskrit: yat tad ucyati kāntāraṃ mahat saṃsāra eva saḥ vanaṃ durgaṃ hi yat tv etat saṃsāragahanaṃ hi tat
english: That great wilderness of which it speaks — that indeed is the round of existence; and this impassable forest is the thicket of worldly being.

sanskrit: ye ca te kathitā vyālā vyādhayas te prakīrtitāḥ yā sā nārī bṛhatkāyā adhitiṣṭhati tatra vai tām āhus tu jarāṃ prājñā varṇarūpavināśinīm
english: Those beasts of prey that were told of are declared to be the diseases; and that woman of vast frame who stands over the place — her the wise call Old Age, destroyer of complexion and of beauty.

sanskrit: yas tatra kūpo nṛpate sa tu dehaḥ śarīriṇām yas tatra vasate 'dhastān mahāhiḥ kāla eva saḥ antakaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ dehināṃ sarvahāry asau
english: That well, O king, is the body of embodied beings; and the great serpent that dwells below within it is Time itself — the Ender of all creatures, who carries off every living thing.

sanskrit: kūpamadhye ca yā jātā vallī yatra sa mānavaḥ pratāne lambate sā tu jīvitāśā śarīriṇām
english: And that creeper grown within the well, by whose tendrils the man hangs suspended — that is the hope of life in embodied beings.

sanskrit: sa yas tu kūpavīnāhe taṃ vṛkṣaṃ parisarpati ṣaḍvaktraḥ kuñjaro rājan sa tu saṃvatsaraḥ smṛtaḥ mukhāni ṛtavo māsāḥ pādā dvādaśa kīrtitāḥ
english: That six-faced elephant which creeps about the tree at the rim of the well, O king, is held to be the year; its faces are the seasons, and its twelve feet are declared to be the months.

sanskrit: ye tu vṛkṣaṃ nikṛntanti mūṣakāḥ satatotthitāḥ rātryahāni tu tāny āhur bhūtānāṃ paricintakāḥ ye te madhukarās tatra kāmās te parikīrtitāḥ
english: The mice that gnaw the tree away, ever at their work — those, the ponderers upon beings declare, are the nights and the days; and the bees there are proclaimed to be the desires.

sanskrit: yās tu tā bahuśo dhārāḥ sravanti madhunisravam tāṃs tu kāmarasān vidyād yatra majjanti mānavāḥ
english: Those many trickling streams that flow with the oozing honey — let them be known as the savors of desire, in which men sink and drown.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃsāracakrasya parivṛttiṃ sma ye viduḥ te vai saṃsāracakrasya pāśāṃś chindanti vai budhāḥ
english: Those wise ones who thus have understood the turning of the wheel of existence — they indeed cut through the bonds of the wheel of existence.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca aho 'bhihitam ākhyānaṃ bhavatā tattvadarśinā bhūya eva tu me harṣaḥ śrotuṃ vāgamṛtaṃ tava
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Ah, well has the tale been told by you who behold the truth! Yet greater still is my joy to go on hearing the nectar of your speech.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca śṛṇu bhūyaḥ pravakṣyāmi mārgasyaitasya vistaram yac chrutvā vipramucyante saṃsārebhyo vicakṣaṇāḥ
english: Vidura said: Hear once more; I shall expound the fullness of this path, hearing which the discerning are wholly freed from the rounds of existence.

sanskrit: yathā tu puruṣo rājan dīrgham adhvānam āsthitaḥ kva cit kva cic chramāt sthātā kurute vāsam eva vā
english: Just as a man, O king, who has set out upon a long road, halts here and there from weariness, or makes his lodging for a while —

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃsāraparyāye garbhavāseṣu bhārata kurvanti durbudhā vāsaṃ mucyante tatra paṇḍitāḥ
english: so, in the turning round of existence, in dwellings within the womb, O Bhārata, the foolish make their lodging, while the wise win release therefrom.

sanskrit: tasmād adhvānam evaitam āhuḥ śāstravido janāḥ yat tu saṃsāragahanaṃ vanam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: Therefore those versed in the scriptures call this very thing a road; and the thicket of worldly existence the thoughtful call a forest.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ lokasamāvarto martyānāṃ bharatarṣabha carāṇāṃ sthāvarāṇāṃ ca gṛdhyet tatra na paṇḍitaḥ
english: This is the world's revolving round for mortals, O bull of the Bhāratas, for moving and unmoving things alike; therein the wise man should not be greedy.

sanskrit: śārīrā mānasāś caiva martyānāṃ ye tu vyādhayaḥ pratyakṣāś ca parokṣāś ca te vyālāḥ kathitā budhaiḥ
english: The diseases of mortals, whether of the body or of the mind, whether seen or unseen — these are declared by the wise to be the beasts of prey.

sanskrit: kliśyamānāś ca tair nityaṃ hanyamānāś ca bhārata svakarmabhir mahāvyālair nodvijanty alpabuddhayaḥ
english: Tormented by them without end and slain, O Bhārata, by those great beasts that are their own deeds, the dull of understanding are still not made afraid.

sanskrit: athāpi tair vimucyeta vyādhibhiḥ puruṣo nṛpa āvṛṇoty eva taṃ paścāj jarā rūpavināśinī
english: And even should a man be freed from those diseases, O king, Old Age that destroys all beauty closes about him in the end.

sanskrit: śabdarūparasasparśair gandhaiś ca vividhair api majjamānaṃ mahāpaṅke nirālambe samantataḥ
english: By sound, form, taste, and touch, and by manifold scents as well, he sinks into a great mire that has no foothold on any side.

sanskrit: saṃvatsarartavo māsāḥ pakṣāhorātrasaṃdhayaḥ krameṇāsya pralumpanti rūpam āyus tathaiva ca
english: Years, seasons, months, fortnights, days and nights, and their junctures, one after another plunder away his beauty and his span of life as well.

sanskrit: ete kālasya nidhayo naitāñ jānanti durbudhāḥ atrābhilikhitāny āhuḥ sarvabhūtāni karmaṇā
english: These are the treasure-stores of Time, which the dull of mind do not know; herein, they say, all creatures are inscribed by their deeds.

sanskrit: rathaṃ śarīraṃ bhūtānāṃ sattvam āhus tu sārathim indriyāṇi hayān āhuḥ karma buddhiś ca raśmayaḥ
english: The body of beings they call the chariot; the inner being they call the charioteer; the senses they call the horses, and action and intellect the reins.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ hayānāṃ yo vegaṃ dhāvatām anudhāvati sa tu saṃsāracakre 'smiṃś cakravat parivartate
english: Whoever runs after the rushing speed of those galloping horses revolves, like a wheel, upon this wheel of worldly existence.

sanskrit: yas tān yamayate buddhyā sa yantā na nivartate yāmyam āhū rathaṃ hy enaṃ muhyante yena durbudhāḥ
english: But he who reins them in by the intellect — that driver turns not back again; for this chariot, by which the dull of mind are bewildered, they call the chariot of Yama.

sanskrit: sa caitat prāpnute rājan yat tvaṃ prāpto narādhipa rājyanāśaṃ suhṛnnāśaṃ sutanāśaṃ ca bhārata
english: And such a one comes to that very thing which you have come to, O lord of men: the loss of kingdom, the loss of friends, and the loss of sons, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: anutarṣulam evaitad duḥkhaṃ bhavati bhārata sādhuḥ paramaduḥkhānāṃ duḥkhabhaiṣajyam ācaret
english: This grief is but a craving renewed without end, O Bhārata; the good man, amid the greatest sorrows, should apply the medicine of sorrow.

sanskrit: na vikramo na cāpy artho na mitraṃ na suhṛjjanaḥ tathonmocayate duḥkhād yathātmā sthirasaṃyamaḥ
english: Neither valor nor wealth, nor a friend, nor the company of well-wishers, sets one free from sorrow as does a self made steadfast in self-restraint.

sanskrit: tasmān maitraṃ samāsthāya śīlam āpadya bhārata damas tyāgo 'pramādaś ca te trayo brahmaṇo hayāḥ
english: Therefore, taking your stand upon friendliness and entering into good conduct, O Bhārata — self-control, renunciation, and vigilance: these three are the horses of Brahman.

sanskrit: śīlaraśmisamāyukte sthito yo mānase rathe tyaktvā mṛtyubhayaṃ rājan brahmalokaṃ sa gacchati
english: He who stands upon the chariot of the mind, yoked with the reins of good conduct, casting off the fear of death, O king, goes to the world of Brahman.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vidurasya tu tad vākyaṃ niśamya kurusattamaḥ putraśokābhisaṃtaptaḥ papāta bhuvi mūrchitaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: But hearing those words of Vidura, the best of the Kurus, consumed with grief for his sons, fell to the ground in a swoon.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā patitaṃ bhūmau niḥsaṃjñaṃ prekṣya bāndhavāḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaś caiva kṣattā ca viduras tathā
english: Seeing him thus fallen senseless upon the earth, his kinsmen, and Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana, and the Kṣattṛ, Vidura,

sanskrit: saṃjayaḥ suhṛdaś cānye dvāḥsthā ye cāsya saṃmatāḥ jalena sukhaśītena tālavṛntaiś ca bhārata
english: and Saṃjaya, and other well-wishers, and the doorkeepers held in his esteem — with pleasantly cool water and with palm-leaf fans, O Bhārata,

sanskrit: paspṛśuś ca karair gātraṃ vījamānāś ca yatnataḥ anvāsan suciraṃ kālaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ tathāgatam
english: touched his limbs with their hands and, fanning him with care, attended for a long while upon Dhṛtarāṣṭra brought to such a pass.

sanskrit: atha dīrghasya kālasya labdhasaṃjño mahīpatiḥ vilalāpa ciraṃ kālaṃ putrādhibhir abhiplutaḥ
english: Then, after a long while, the lord of the earth regained his senses and lamented for a long time, overwhelmed by anguish for his sons.

sanskrit: dhig astu khalu mānuṣyaṃ mānuṣye ca parigraham yatomūlāni duḥkhāni saṃbhavanti muhur muhuḥ
english: Fie, indeed, upon this human estate, and upon the holding of possessions in human life, from which the sorrows arise that have their root therein, again and again!

sanskrit: putranāśe 'rthanāśe ca jñātisaṃbandhinām api prāpyate sumahad duḥkhaṃ viṣāgnipratimaṃ vibho
english: In the loss of sons, in the loss of wealth, and of kinsmen and relations too, a most exceeding grief is met with, like poison and like fire, O mighty one.

sanskrit: yena dahyanti gātrāṇi yena prajñā vinaśyati yenābhibhūtaḥ puruṣo maraṇaṃ bahu manyate
english: By it the limbs are burned, by it understanding is destroyed; overcome by it, a man holds death itself to be a thing much to be desired.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ vyasanaṃ prāptaṃ mayā bhāgyaviparyayāt tac caivāhaṃ kariṣyāmi adyaiva dvijasattama
english: This is the calamity that has come upon me through the reversal of my fortune; and this very thing I shall do this very day, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: ity uktvā tu mahātmānaṃ pitaraṃ brahmavittamam dhṛtarāṣṭro 'bhavan mūḍhaḥ śokaṃ ca paramaṃ gataḥ abhūc ca tūṣṇīṃ rājāsau dhyāyamāno mahīpate
english: Having spoken thus to his great-souled father, foremost among the knowers of Brahman, Dhṛtarāṣṭra grew bewildered and passed into the uttermost grief; and that king fell silent, sunk in brooding thought, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ prabhuḥ putraśokābhisaṃtaptaṃ putraṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Hearing that speech of his, the lord Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana spoke these words to his son, who was consumed with grief for his own sons.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra mahābāho yat tvāṃ vakṣyāmi tac chṛṇu śrutavān asi medhāvī dharmārthakuśalas tathā
english: O mighty-armed Dhṛtarāṣṭra, hear what I shall say to you. Learned you are, and wise, and skilled alike in dharma and in worldly aims.

sanskrit: na te 'sty aviditaṃ kiṃ cid veditavyaṃ paraṃtapa anityatāṃ hi martyānāṃ vijānāsi na saṃśayaḥ
english: There is nothing worth knowing that is unknown to you, O scorcher of foes; for the impermanence of mortals you understand, beyond all doubt.

sanskrit: adhruve jīvaloke ca sthāne vāśāśvate sati jīvite maraṇānte ca kasmāc chocasi bhārata
english: When the world of the living is unstable, and one's station unenduring, and life itself ends in death — why then do you grieve, O Bhārata?
